geogcomments: Sao Pedro da Torre (SPT) is located in northwest Portugal, close to the border with Spain. The outcrop occurs in a 4 km wide depression between Porrino (Spain) and V.N. Cerveira (Portugal), and was exposed due to the A3 highway construction.
lithdescript: The outcrop consists of clays, lignite layers, sands and gravel.
primary_reference: M. Vieira, R. Zetter, and F. Grímsson, T. Denk. 2022. Niche evolution versus niche conservatism and habitat loss determine persistence and extirpation in late Neogene European Fagaceae. Quaternary Science Reviews 300
lithdescript.1: The outcrop consists of clays, lignite layers, sands and gravel.
geology_comments: A study of the pollen content from the clays suggests mixed deciduous-evergreen broadleaved and conifer forests that thrived under humid warm-temperate climates in that region.
collection_comments: Standard laboratory processing for palynomorphs with HCl and HF for acid maceration followed by sieving. Final residues were diluted in liquid glycerine and mounted on slides.

collection_name: Headwaters of the Rio Chico, Lago Colhue Huapi
geogcomments: The palynoflora was recovered from sediments overlyingan erosion surface at the top of the Lago Colhué (Casal et al., 2015) at the headwaters of the Río Chico (designated as the holostratotype of the unit) (Figs. 1,2.1–3).
stratcomments: At the headwaters of the Río Chico, a basalt flow with a radiometric age of 67.31 ± 0.55 Ma (La Angostura Basalt) lies on top of the Lago Colhué Huapi Formation (Clyde et al., 2014).\r\nThe palynoflora from the studied levels at the headwaters of the Río Chico, in the Golfo San Jorge Basin, includes austral Maastrichtian key species such as Quadraplanus brossus and Tubulifloridites lilliei. The assemblage is also typified by paleotropical Maastrichtian markers such as Buttinia andreevi and Gabonisporis vigourouxii. All above mentioned taxa characterize late Maastrichtian assemblages and become extinct at the Cretaceous/Paleogene boundary thus suggesting a late Maastrichtian age for the studied palynoflora.
lithdescript: The Lago Colhué Huapi Formation, widely distributed in the basin, is predominantly composed of reddish mudstones of fluvial origin. According to the position in the basin, the\r\nLago Colhué Huapi Formation overlies the Bajo Barreal Formation and underlies the marine Danian Salamanca Formation or the tuffaceous levels of the Laguna Palacios Formation (Casal et al., 2015). In the upper part of the Lago Colhué Huapi Formation, at the headwaters of the Río Chico, an erosion surface underlies sedimentary rocks including the fertile levels.
primary_reference: P. Vallati, G. Casal, and N. Foix, J. Allard, A. De Sosa Tomas, M. Calo. 2016. First report of a Maastrichtian palynoflora from the Golfo San Jorge Basin, central Patagonia, Argentina. Ameghiniana 53(4):495-505
lithdescript.1: The Lago Colhué Huapi Formation, widely distributed in the basin, is predominantly composed of reddish mudstones of fluvial origin. According to the position in the basin, the\r\nLago Colhué Huapi Formation overlies the Bajo Barreal Formation and underlies the marine Danian Salamanca Formation or the tuffaceous levels of the Laguna Palacios Formation (Casal et al., 2015). In the upper part of the Lago Colhué Huapi Formation, at the headwaters of the Río Chico, an erosion surface underlies sedimentary rocks including the fertile levels.
geology_comments: Aquatic fern spores (Azolla spp.; Ariadnaesporites micromedusus) together with lycophytes and algal elements suggest the local existence of a freshwater body and a warm climate. Particularly, zygospores of the green filamentous algae Zygnemataceae such as Catinipollis geiseltalensis Krutzsch, 1966 imply warm, shallow and low energy freshwaters (Scafati et al., 2009; Bowman et al., 2014).
collection_comments: The samples were processed following standard palynological methods including maceration with hydrochloric and hydrofluoric acids for carbonate and silicate removal. A brief oxidation of the residue with nitric acid was performed in order to improve the results. The organic residue was mounted on microscope slides using glycerine jelly. The samples were studied with a Carl Zeiss KF 2 microscope and the microphotographs were obtained with a digital Nikon Coolpix P2 camera at the Biostratigraphic Laboratory of the Universidad Nacional de la Patagonia San Juan Bosco. The relative abundance of palynomorphs mentioned in the analysis of the palynoflora was based on counts of 300 specimens.
taxonomy_comments: UNPSJB, Universidad de la Patagonia “San Juan Bosco”, colección de Paleovertebrados, Chubut, Argentina

geogcomments: Cerro del Hadro at the headwaters of the Río Chico in the Golfo San Jorge Basin (45°37′20.17″S, 68°26′35.42″W).
stratcomments: Uppermost Lago Colhué Huapi Formation. Geological studies—particularly those of palynomorphs—support a late Maastrichtian age, probably close to the Cretaceous/Paleogene boundary, for the stratigraphic horizon in question (Vallati et al., 2016, 2020).
lithdescript: The outcrop known as Cerro del Hadro is well exposed on the southern margin of the Chico river. The sequence is 150 m thick and has the typical lithological alternation that characterizes the Lago Colhué Huapi Formation. It includes an irregular erosion surface (local unconformity) of concave geometry in the upper part. Its sedimentary filling is more than 20 m thick. lithdescript: The sedimentary deposits that are partially outcropping in Corral de Piedra include alternation of claystones, siltstones, and sandstones. The mudstone deposits that include the palynomorphs are massive to horizontally laminated, 0.2–3.2 m thick, interpreted as the deposit of suspended particles in a dilute flow. The sandstones are medium to fine grain, gray-colored and with a diffuse horizontal lamination. This sandstone bed has a flat base and top and is 0.18–0.9 m thick, being interpreted as a traction deposit in low flow conditions.

lithdescript: La Anita Formation is characterized by fine- to medium-grained yellowish sandstone bodies with trough-cross stratification, tabular fine dark laminated organic-rich claystones, and channelized sandstone bodies with trough-cross stratification and abundant carbonaceous material.
primary_reference: P. E. Santamarina, V. D. Barreda, and D. Moyano Paz, C. Tettamanti, A. Iglesias, D. G. Poiré, A. N. Varela. 2020. Palynoflora from the La Anita Formation (Maastrichtian), Austral-Magallanes Basin, Argentina. Revista del Museo Argentino de Ciencias Naturales 22(1):47-56
lithdescript.1: La Anita Formation is characterized by fine- to medium-grained yellowish sandstone bodies with trough-cross stratification, tabular fine dark laminated organic-rich claystones, and channelized sandstone bodies with trough-cross stratification and abundant carbonaceous material.
geology_comments: The La Anita Formation was interpreted as a delta system with vertical variation on the relative roles of processes affecting it; thus, a wave-dominated lower unit and a fluvio-dominated upper unit were defined by Moyano Paz et al. (2018).
collection_comments: The specimens are stored at the paleobotanical collection of the Museo Regional Provincial “Padre Jesús Molina”, Rio Gallegos, Santa Cruz Province (acronym MPM-Pb).\r\n\r\nSamples were processed following standard palynological techniques, and mounted in a glycerol mounting medium. The observations were made under a Leica DM2500 light microscope and the photographs were taken with a Leica DFC295 digital camera. Specimen locations refer to England Finder coordinates. In order to obtain the relative abundance of plant groups, counts of at least 300 individuals were conducted. Broken individuals were not counted, and tetrads and polyads were counted as one individual.

geogcomments: Fifteen wood remains were collected from the Puntudo Chico Formation at the Estancia María de las Nieves locality, Chubut Province, Argentina. Collection was carried out at a site located at the north of the main buildings of the Estancia (42°25′36″S 66°19′51″W).
stratcomments: The Puntudo Chico Formation is commonly regarded as Campanian–Maastrichtian. Vera et al. (2019) briefly discussed the age of the unit, comparing its fossil record with other Late Cretaceous to Danian Patagonian floristic assemblages, and suggested a middle to upper Campanian to Maastrichtian age for this unit. Recently, Clyde et al. (2021) obtained absolute ages using detrital zircons from rocks located at the top of the Puntudo Chico Formation, immediately below the base of the La Colonia Formation. An age of 71.71 ± 0.33 My obtained by these authors implying that the upper limit of the Puntudo Chico Formation in the area can be constrained to the lowermost Maastrichtian.
lithdescript: The Puntudo Chico Formation comprises sandstones and conglomerates deposited in a\r\nhigh energy fluvial system, geographically restricted to the Chubut Province (Pesce, 1978;\r\nLapido & Page, 1978; Page, 1987; Anselmi et al., 2004; Silva Nieto et al., 2020). Outcrops of this unit have been considered by some authors as a lower section of the La Colonia Formation (e.g., Pascual et al., 2000; Gasparini et al., 2015), but its nature as a separate lithostratigraphic unit is currently accepted (e.g., Vera et al., 2019; Clyde et al., 2021).
primary_reference: E. I. Vera, V. S. Perez Loinaze, and M. Llorens, M. G. Passalia. 2024. New paleobotanical data from the Puntudo Chico Formation (uppermost Cretaceous), Chubut Province, Argentina. Revista del Museo Argentino de Ciencias Naturales 26(1):1-10
lithdescript.1: The Puntudo Chico Formation comprises sandstones and conglomerates deposited in a\r\nhigh energy fluvial system, geographically restricted to the Chubut Province (Pesce, 1978;\r\nLapido & Page, 1978; Page, 1987; Anselmi et al., 2004; Silva Nieto et al., 2020). Outcrops of this unit have been considered by some authors as a lower section of the La Colonia Formation (e.g., Pascual et al., 2000; Gasparini et al., 2015), but its nature as a separate lithostratigraphic unit is currently accepted (e.g., Vera et al., 2019; Clyde et al., 2021).
collection_methods: surface (in situ),chemical,mechanical,peel or thin section,field collection
collection_comments: The fossil woods were thin sectioned in transverse (TS), longitudinal tangential (LTS), and longitudinal radial (LRS) sections, and studied using light microscopy (Olympus BX51). Descriptive terminology used here for conifer woods follows the IAWA list of microscopic features for softwood identification (Richter et al. 2004), with the addition of terms defined in Philippe & Bamford\r\n(2008) and Boura et al. (2021). Pit counting method follows Philippe et al. (2014). Seriation and contiguity indices proposed by Pujana et al. (2016) were also estimated when possible.

collection_comments: Samples were crushed into small fragments and homogenised. collection_comments: The material was scattered, and one drop of hydrochloric acid was added to test for the presence of carbonates. HCl (30%) and HF (45%) were applied successively, and washings were carried out using distilled water until the sample was neutralized after each acid. In some cases, it was necessary to repeat the procedure with HF. Then, they were treated with hot HCl to disaggregate the organic matter and filtered through 25 μm and 10 μm meshes. Gelatin-glycerin and a drop of formalin were used as mounting medium. The palynological study was carried out using a Leica DM 500 optical microscope and an AmScope 14 MPixels video camera. The optical instruments belong to the Palynology and Paleobotany Laboratory of the CICYTTP (CONICET-ENTRE RIOS-UADER) located in Diamante, Entre Ríos. HCl (30%) and HF (45%) were applied successively, and washings were carried out using distilled water until the sample was neutralized after each acid. In some cases, it was necessary to repeat the procedure with HF. Then, they were treated with hot HCl to disaggregate the organic matter and filtered through 25 μm and 10 μm meshes. Gelatin-glycerin and a drop of formalin were used as mounting medium. The palynological study was carried out using a Leica DM 500 optical microscope and an AmScope 14 MPixels video camera. The optical instruments belong to the Palynology and Paleobotany Laboratory of the CICYTTP (CONICET-ENTRE RIOS-UADER) located in Diamante, Entre Ríos. The studied material has been deposited at the Paleopalynology collection of the Palynology and Paleobotany Laboratory at the CICYTTP Research Center (CONICET- ENTRE RIOS-UADER) and was identified under the initials CICYTTP-Pl 1373 to CICYTTP-Pl 1396

In some cases, it was necessary to repeat the procedure with HF. Then, they were treated with hot HCl to disaggregate the organic matter and filtered through 25 μm and 10 μm meshes. Gelatin-glycerin and a drop of formalin were used as mounting medium. The palynological study was carried out using a Leica DM 500 optical microscope and an AmScope 14 MPixels video camera. The optical instruments belong to the Palynology and Paleobotany Laboratory of the CICYTTP (CONICET-ENTRE RIOS-UADER) located in Diamante, Entre Ríos. The studied material has been deposited at the Paleopalynology collection of the Palynology and Paleobotany Laboratory at the CICYTTP Research Center (CONICET- ENTRE RIOS-UADER) and was identified under the initials CICYTTP-Pl 1373 to CICYTTP-Pl 1396

collection_comments: The samples were processed using normal palynological techniques of HCl; HF; short centrifugation with soapy water to remove fines; heavy liwuid separation using a ZnCl2 liquid of 1.8 to 2.2 s.g., or, in same cases, 1.45 s.g. geology_comments: Authors identified two palaeoenvironments designated as P1 and P2. P1 comprised FL1 to FL4, with samples FL2 and FL4 with the minimum taxonomic richness (S-NPP = 1–2), and P2 is comprised by samples FL5 and FL6 with the highest taxonomic richness (S-NPP = 6–7) in the section.\r\nIn contrast to P1, P2 shows an increase in amorphous organic material, including phytoclasts such as cuticles and conductive elements.

geogcomments: The study area is located between two zones: 1, Estancia Laguna Salada (51º 10’ 49’’S, 72º 17’ 23’’O), Cancha Carrera, near Argentina-Chile boundary; and 2, Estancia San José (51º 35’ 11’’S, 72º 24’ 23’’O), Río Turbio zone, Santa Cruz province.
stratcomments: On the other hand, based on the stratigraphic distribution of the dinoflagellate cyst species identified in a preliminary study (Povilauskas & Guler, 2008)—particularly the presence of Isabelidinium sp., Nelsoniella sp., Odontochitina spp., and Palaeocystodinium australinum—along with the angiosperms Nothofagidites saraensis and Peninsulapollis gillii, an age around the Maastrichtian–Danian is suggested.
lithdescript: The Cerro Cazador Formation is composed of fine to medium sandstones, with interbedded calcarenites—partly glauconitic—mudstones, conglomerates, and limestone beds containing remains of pelecypods, gastropods, nautiloids, and ammonoids (Riccardi & Rolleri, 1980).
primary_reference: L. Povilauskas. 2016. Estudio palinológico de la Formación Cerro Cazador (Cretácico tardío) de la Provincia de Santa Cruz, Argentina. Revista Brasileira de Paleontologia 19(1):71-84
lithdescript.1: The Cerro Cazador Formation is composed of fine to medium sandstones, with interbedded calcarenites—partly glauconitic—mudstones, conglomerates, and limestone beds containing remains of pelecypods, gastropods, nautiloids, and ammonoids (Riccardi & Rolleri, 1980).
geology_comments: A preliminary palynological analysis of this sequence (Povilauskas et al., 2006; Povilauskas & Guler, 2008) suggested a nearshore marine depositional environment, very close to the coast, in agreement with earlier interpretations by Herm (1966) and Russo et al. (1980).
collection_comments: Repository: MPM-MP, Museo Regional Provincial “Padre Manuel Jesús Molina”, Río Gallegos, Provincia de Santa Cruz, Argentina.\r\n\r\nThe physicochemical extraction of the palynological content was carried out following standard processing methods using HCl-HF, after which the residue was filtered with 10 and 25 micron meshes. The final slides were mounted in glycerin jelly. A total of 12 samples from the two studied zones of the aforementioned formation were processed, of which 9 (CC1 to CC9, respectively) yielded fertile palynomorphs. These are distributed from the base to the top of the integrated section. The specimens were studied using a Leitz Wetzlar Germany and an Olympus BX51 (Japan) microscope at the Palynology Section, and photographs were taken using both a transmitted light optical microscope and a scanning electron microscope (SEM) at the Museo Argentino de Ciencias Naturales “Bernardino Rivadavia.” A Nikon E4500 digital camera was used for the photographic documentation of the specimens.

geology_comments: A preliminary palynological analysis of this sequence (Povilauskas et al., 2006; Povilauskas & Guler, 2008) suggested a nearshore marine depositional environment, very close to the coast, in agreement with earlier interpretations by Herm (1966) and Russo et al. (1980).
collection_comments: Repository: MPM-MP, Museo Regional Provincial “Padre Manuel Jesús Molina”, Río Gallegos, Provincia de Santa Cruz, Argentina.\r\n\r\nThe physicochemical extraction of the palynological content was carried out following standard processing methods using HCl-HF, after which the residue was filtered with 10 and 25 micron meshes. The final slides were mounted in glycerin jelly. A total of 12 samples from the two studied zones of the aforementioned formation were processed, of which 9 (CC1 to CC9, respectively) yielded fertile palynomorphs. These are distributed from the base to the top of the integrated section. The specimens were studied using a Leitz Wetzlar Germany and an Olympus BX51 (Japan) microscope at the Palynology Section, and photographs were taken using both a transmitted light optical microscope and a scanning electron microscope (SEM) at the Museo Argentino de Ciencias Naturales “Bernardino Rivadavia.” A Nikon E4500 digital camera was used for the photographic documentation of the specimens.

lithdescript.1: The Cerro Cazador Formation is composed of fine to medium sandstones, with interbedded calcarenites—partly glauconitic—mudstones, conglomerates, and limestone beds containing remains of pelecypods, gastropods, nautiloids, and ammonoids (Riccardi & Rolleri, 1980).
geology_comments: A preliminary palynological analysis of this sequence (Povilauskas et al., 2006; Povilauskas & Guler, 2008) suggested a nearshore marine depositional environment, very close to the coast, in agreement with earlier interpretations by Herm (1966) and Russo et al. (1980).
collection_comments: Repository: MPM-MP, Museo Regional Provincial “Padre Manuel Jesús Molina”, Río Gallegos, Provincia de Santa Cruz, Argentina.\r\n\r\nThe physicochemical extraction of the palynological content was carried out following standard processing methods using HCl-HF, after which the residue was filtered with 10 and 25 micron meshes. The final slides were mounted in glycerin jelly. A total of 12 samples from the two studied zones of the aforementioned formation were processed, of which 9 (CC1 to CC9, respectively) yielded fertile palynomorphs. These are distributed from the base to the top of the integrated section. The specimens were studied using a Leitz Wetzlar Germany and an Olympus BX51 (Japan) microscope at the Palynology Section, and photographs were taken using both a transmitted light optical microscope and a scanning electron microscope (SEM) at the Museo Argentino de Ciencias Naturales “Bernardino Rivadavia.” A Nikon E4500 digital camera was used for the photographic documentation of the specimens.

collection_comments: Repository: MPM-MP, Museo Regional Provincial “Padre Manuel Jesús Molina”, Río Gallegos, Provincia de Santa Cruz, Argentina.\r\n\r\nThe physicochemical extraction of the palynological content was carried out following standard processing methods using HCl-HF, after which the residue was filtered with 10 and 25 micron meshes. The final slides were mounted in glycerin jelly. A total of 12 samples from the two studied zones of the aforementioned formation were processed, of which 9 (CC1 to CC9, respectively) yielded fertile palynomorphs. These are distributed from the base to the top of the integrated section. The specimens were studied using a Leitz Wetzlar Germany and an Olympus BX51 (Japan) microscope at the Palynology Section, and photographs were taken using both a transmitted light optical microscope and a scanning electron microscope (SEM) at the Museo Argentino de Ciencias Naturales “Bernardino Rivadavia.” A Nikon E4500 digital camera was used for the photographic documentation of the specimens.

geology_comments: As a result, it is interpreted that the entire unit was deposited under a marginal coastal regime, probably shallow, under warm and at least locally humid climatic conditions (Povilauskas, 2013).
collection_comments: Repository: MPM-MP, Museo Regional Provincial “Padre Manuel Jesús Molina”, Río Gallegos, Provincia de Santa Cruz, Argentina.\r\nPalynological extraction was carried out following conventional physical and chemical extraction methods for palynology (HCl-HF), and the resulting residue was filtered using +10 and +25 micron meshes. The final preparations were mounted in glycerin jelly. Specimens were studied using a Leitz Wetzlar Germany microscope and an Olympus BX51 from the Paleopalynology Section, and were photographed using both a transmitted light optical microscope and a scanning electron microscope (SEM) at the Argentine Museum of Natural Sciences 'Bernardino Rivadavia'. For photographic documentation of the specimens, a Nikon E4500 digital camera was used. The semi-natural classification system proposed by Pocock (1962) was followed, using morphotaxa at the genus and species level.

collection_comments: Repository: MPM-MP, Museo Regional Provincial “Padre Manuel Jesús Molina”, Río Gallegos, Provincia de Santa Cruz, Argentina.\r\nPalynological extraction was carried out following conventional physical and chemical extraction methods for palynology (HCl-HF), and the resulting residue was filtered using +10 and +25 micron meshes. collection_comments: Repository: MPM-MP, Museo Regional Provincial “Padre Manuel Jesús Molina”, Río Gallegos, Provincia de Santa Cruz, Argentina.\r\nPalynological extraction was carried out following conventional physical and chemical extraction methods for palynology (HCl-HF), and the resulting residue was filtered using +10 and +25 micron meshes. The final preparations were mounted in glycerin jelly. Specimens were studied using a Leitz Wetzlar Germany microscope and an Olympus BX51 from the Paleopalynology Section, and were photographed using both a transmitted light optical microscope and a scanning electron microscope (SEM) at the Argentine Museum of Natural Sciences 'Bernardino Rivadavia'. For photographic documentation of the specimens, a Nikon E4500 digital camera was used. The semi-natural classification system proposed by Pocock (1962) was followed, using morphotaxa at the genus and species level.

collection_comments: Repository: MPM-MP, Museo Regional Provincial “Padre Manuel Jesús Molina”, Río Gallegos, Provincia de Santa Cruz, Argentina.\r\nPalynological extraction was carried out following conventional physical and chemical extraction methods for palynology (HCl-HF), and the resulting residue was filtered using +10 and +25 micron meshes. primary_reference: L. K. Povilauskas. 2010. Palinología del entorno cretácico/paleógeno del SO de la provincia de Santa Cruz: significado estratigráfico y paleoambiental. Universidad Nacional de La Plata. Facultad de Ciencias Naturales y Museo de La Plata
lithdescript.1: The Cerro Dorotea Formation  is composed of psammites and psephites, with interbedded coquinas, characteristic of inner shelf marine environments with limited or no connection to the open sea.
geology_comments: It could be a characteristic of inner shelf marine environments with limited or no connection to the open sea.
collection_comments: Repository: MPM-MP, Museo Regional Provincial “Padre Manuel Jesús Molina”, Río Gallegos, Provincia de Santa Cruz, Argentina.\r\nPalynological extraction was carried out following conventional physical and chemical extraction methods for palynology (HCl-HF), and the resulting residue was filtered using +10 and +25 micron meshes. The final preparations were mounted in glycerin jelly. Specimens were studied using a Leitz Wetzlar Germany microscope and an Olympus BX51 from the Paleopalynology Section, and were photographed using both a transmitted light optical microscope and a scanning electron microscope (SEM) at the Argentine Museum of Natural Sciences 'Bernardino Rivadavia'. For photographic documentation of the specimens, a Nikon E4500 digital camera was used. The semi-natural classification system proposed by Pocock (1962) was followed, using morphotaxa at the genus and species level.

geogcomments: Specimens studied in the present work were obtained from exposures of the Chorrillo Formation, at the southern margin of the Lago Argentino, Santa Cruz Province, Argentina.
primary_reference: V. S. Perez Loinaze, E. I. Vera, and D. Moyano-Paz, M. D. Coronel, M. Manabe, T. Tsuihiji, F. E. Novas. 2023. Maastrichtian palynological assemblages from the Chorrillo Formation,\r\nPatagonia, Argentina. Review of Palaeobotany and Palynology 314(104893):1-17
collectors: E. Vera, D. Moyano-Paz, M. Coronel
collection_comments: MPM-Pal 21837, Museo Padre Molina, Argentina\r\nAn exhaustive sampling was carried out from the lower and middle part of the Chorrillo Formation (Fig. 2). Sixty-two samples for palynological analysis were collected and processed using standard palynological techniques for extraction and concentration of palynomorphs (Phipps and Playford, 1984), of which sixty samples provided material for palynological studies (Fig. 2). The organic residue was sieved using 20-μm and 10-μm mesh and mounted in permanent slides following the methods of Noetinger et al. (2017). Observations were made with an Olympus BX-51 microscope while photographs were taken with an Olympus DP25 digital camera. Coordinates of the illustrated specimens are given using England Finder. The slides are deposited in the Museo Regional Provincial “Padre Molina”, Santa Cruz province, Argentina (MPM).
taxonomy_comments: Is part of a total of 44 spore species, 55 angiosperm, and 28 gymnosperm pollen grains, were identified.

The slides are deposited in the Museo Regional Provincial “Padre Molina”, Santa Cruz province, Argentina (MPM).

collection_comments: MPM-Pal 21834\r\nPalynomorphs were extracted and concentrated from fragments of rocks obtained from both Megafloral levels by treating them with HCl 38% and HF 45% using standard palynological techniques (Phipps and Playford, 1984) and also without prior crushing, and then sieved using 20 mm and 10 mm meshes, as well as 80 mm and 500 mm meshes, to obtain the larger fractions, i.e., organic macrofossils (sensu Pole, 2007). Individual cuticles and other remains were also collected from these fractions under a binocular microscope and mounted on microscope slides. The organic residues were sieved using an 80 mm mesh and mounted on permanent slides, and then explored for cuticles and other remains. Treatments of rocks from Megafloral level 2 with HCl 38% and HF 45% did not result in recoverable organic remains.\r\nAll studied specimens are housed in the Museo Regional Padre Jesús Molina (Río Gallegos, Santa Cruz Province), under MPM-PB (hand samples) and MPM-Pal (Palynological slides and SEM stubs) acronyms.
taxonomy_comments: The studied sample preserves a rich and diverse palynoflora composed of a total of 15 spore species, 23 angiosperm pollen grains, and 19 gymnosperm pollen grains

stratcomments: The fossil-bearing levels of silicified logs are here referred to deposits of the Allen Formation\r\n(middle-upper Campanian to lower Maastrichtian, Malargüe Group).
lithdescript: The SGm facies (Fig. 3C) is composed of massive, coarse-grained and gravelly to sabulitic sandstones. This facies is texturally and compositionally immature, moderate to poorly sorted, with subangular to subrounded clasts and composed predominantly by\r\ngrains of quartz, basic vulcanites and acidic porphyries. This facies are developed in tabular bodies with an erosive base and laterally wedged; reaching up to 100 cm in thickness. Internally, also it may exhibit crude stratification and normal grading.
primary_reference: M. Passalia, A. Garrido, and A. Iglesias, E. Vera. 2023. The Valcheta Petrified Forest (Upper Cretaceous), northern Patagonia, Argentina: A geological and paleobotanical survey. Cretaceous Research 142(78):105395

geology_comments: In general terms, the set of facies described indicates the action of unidirectional flows of moderate to high energy, related to water currents that made possible the transport of coarse sedimentary load under the domain of tractive processes (Harms and Fahnestock, 1965; Allen, 1982). The arrangement of the lithofacial association suggests the development of gravelly bed forms associated with frontal accretion fluvial bars, a macroform that characterizes braided fluvial systems (Miall, 1977, 1996; Collinson, 1986; Sanchez-Moya and Sopeña, 2010).

geogcomments: Studied wood remains were collected from the lower section of the Puntudo Chico Formation at the El Quiosco locality (43º20'53''S. 67º48'W) in the vicinities of the El Mirasol village, Chubut Province, Argentina.
stratcomments: The Puntudo Chico Formation is commonly regarded as Campanian–Maastrichtian. Vera et al. (2019) briefly discussed the age of the unit, comparing its fossil record with other Late Cretaceous to Danian Patagonian floristic assemblages, and suggested a middle to upper Campanian to Maastrichtian age for this unit. Recently, Clyde et al. (2021) obtained absolute ages using detrital zircons from rocks located at the top of the Puntudo Chico Formation, immediately below the base of the La Colonia Formation. An age of 71.71 ± 0.33 My obtained by these authors implying that the upper limit of the Puntudo Chico Formation in the area can be constrained to the lowermost Maastrichtian.
lithdescript: The Puntudo Chico Formation consists mostly of sandstones and conglomerates deposited in a high energy fluvial system (Lapido and Page, 1978; Pesce, 1978; Page, 1987; Anselmi et al., 2004).
primary_reference: E. Vera, V. Perez Loinaze, and M. Llorens, M. Paez, M. Passalia. 2019. Fossil woods with coniferalean affinities from the Upper Cretaceous (Campanian–Maastrichtian) Puntudo Chico Formation, Chubut Province, Argentina. Cretaceous Research 99(78):321-333
lithdescript.1: The Puntudo Chico Formation consists mostly of sandstones and conglomerates deposited in a high energy fluvial system (Lapido and Page, 1978; Pesce, 1978; Page, 1987; Anselmi et al., 2004).

collection_comments: All specimens are housed in the paleobotanical collection of the Museo Paleontológico Egidio Feruglio (Trelew, Argentina), under the MPEF-PB acronym. The fossil woods were thin-sectioned in transverse (TS), longitudinal tangential (TLS) and longitudinal radial (RLS) sections, and studied using light Microscopy (Olympus BX51) and Scanning Electronic Microscopy (SEM, Philips XL30 TMP). At least 25 measures were taken, and the mean is provided, along maximum and minimum measure observed.

collection_comments: In CHM, 6 samples labeled CHM923-928 were collected from the lower 30 m of grey mudstones located above the basal sandstone of the La Colonia Formation (Fig. S2). The samples were mechanically disaggregated and treated with hydrofluoric acid (70%) and hydrochloric acid (30%). The residue was decanted and washed several times, and then filtered with 150 mm sieves to separate out megaspores and 10 mm sieves for pollen/spore analyses. For light microscopy (LM) observations, the residues were mounted on slides with glycerin jelly. For quantitative analyses a minimum of 300 palynomorphs were counted per slide. LM observations were made with a Nikon Eclipse 80i microscope coupled with a Nikon DS-L4 camera (Nikon Corp., Minato, Tokyo, Japan) at the Museo Paleontológico Egidio Feruglio (MEF) Trelew, Chubut Province, Argentina.

The residue was decanted and washed several times, and then filtered with 150 mm sieves to separate out megaspores and 10 mm sieves for pollen/spore analyses. For light microscopy (LM) observations, the residues were mounted on slides with glycerin jelly. For quantitative analyses a minimum of 300 palynomorphs were counted per slide. LM observations were made with a Nikon Eclipse 80i microscope coupled with a Nikon DS-L4 camera (Nikon Corp., Minato, Tokyo, Japan) at the Museo Paleontológico Egidio Feruglio (MEF) Trelew, Chubut Province, Argentina.

geogcomments: The Cerro Buitre Norte (CBN) section (base at S42.97034, W67.54350, WGS84 datum) is the primary stratigraphic section studied here. The Cerro Buitre Norte section (also known colloquially as the “Plesiosaurio” section) represents one of the longest and most continuous exposures of the La Colonia Formation in the region, especially for the middle-upper parts of the unit. The lower 125 m of the Cerro Buitre Norte section was sampled for this study and spans the middle-upper La Colonia and lower Cerro Bororó formations. The contact between the La Colonia and Cerro Bororó formations occurs at the 108-m level in the section and is marked by a distinct red bed at the top of the La Colonia Formation suggesting slowed deposition or a hiatus of some duration at that time. The Cerro Buitre Norte section is located ~2 km to the southeast of the sections “Norte de Cerro Bayo 1” and “Norte Cerro Bayo 2” presented in Gasparini et al. (2015).
stratcomments: La Colonia Formation is located between the Telsen and Sierra Rosada (Puesto Pintihueque) regions along the plateau border, in Chubut Province, Argentina.\r\n
lithdescript: The base of the La Colonia Formation in the Mirasol Creek area is represented by a ravinement surface, over which shoreface deposits were deposited, similar to the Telsen area (Navarro et al., 2008, 2012; Guler et al., 2014; Borel et al., 2016). The overlying facies are constituted by muddy and heterolithic deposits, arranged in a continuous, prograding tidal succession, as described in previous studies (Guler et al., 2014; Gasparini et al., 2015; Borel et al., 2016). The base of the red siltstone located in the upper Cerro Buitre Norte section, here considered as the top of the La Colonia Formation, is a surface probably related to a pause in sedimentation, before the deposition of the overlying Cerro Bororó Formation. Besides these basal and uppermost key surfaces, no evident discontinuities are present within the studied sections of the La Colonia Formation in this area.

geogcomments: Lago Cardiel, Santa Cruz province
stratcomments: The Cardiel Formation lacks isotopic dates and diagnostic fossils until now. According to stratigraphic relationships, Riccardi and Rolleri (1980) considered a Coniacian–Maastrichtian age, while Ramos (1982) a Cenomanian age. Riccardi and Rolleri (1980) and Giacosa et al. (2012) correlated the Cardiel Formation with the Pari Aike Formation, exposed 60 km south of Cardiel Lake. Exposures of the last unit at Viedma Lake and Tres Lagos region were mapped as the Mata Amarilla Formation (Varela et al. 2012a), which is taken as Cenomanian (96.2 ± 0.71 Mya) according to a U/Pb date of detrital zircons (Varela et al. 2012b).
lithdescript: The Cardiel Formation is a volcaniclastic succession including massive vitric tuffs and bentonites, cross-bedded or rippled tuffaceous sandstones, and subordinately pyroclastic mudstones, claystones, and scarce fine conglomerates (Ramos 1982, Andreis et al. 2007, Panza et al. 2018). Few finning-upward cycles (3–7 m thick), from coarse-grained sandstones or fine conglomerate beds with erosive base to tuffaceous mudstones and bentonites occur in the lower and in the uppermost section. Altered glass shards and pumice fragments of rhyolitic composition are abundant. Their proportion increases towards the top of the unit.

geogcomments: Fossil woods were found at the Estancia Las Violetas locality (Salamanca Formation), Chubut Province, Argentina. lithdescript:
[Bonebed 4] comprises a finely laminated, organic-rich claystone and is completely devoid of interspersed quartz grains."
Bed 1: "Asymmetrical cyclite (more than 4 m thick). At the base: yellow—brown coarse-grained poorly sorted sandstones—chlidolites (more than 1 m thick) with an admixture of granitoid detritus and gravel, with infrequent interbeds (up to 5—10 cm thick) of dark gray, black, coaly, slightly layered massive siltstones"
Bed 3: "Dark gray sandy siltstone (up to 1 m thick), with hardly discernible horizontal texture, with beds of carbonized vegetative detritus"
Bed 4: A marking layer (5–7 cm thick) of whitish massive dense ash tuffite with conchoidal fracture, with bioclastic rock"
Bed 5: Yellowish fine—medium-grained, poorly sorted massive sandstone—chlidolite (5–10 cm thick) with an admixture of granite gravel and gruss and silt stone lenses."
Bed 6: "Brown, yellowish siltstones (5–10 cm thick), with Liesegang rings, with complex tangled fibrous, landslide texture."
Bed 7: "Yellowish fine—medium-grained sandstone—chlidolite (5–10 cm thick), with chaotically scattered granite gruss and carbonized woods."
Bed 8: "Brownish fulvous siltstones (5–10 cm thick), with an indistinct horizontal texture"
Bed 9: "Brownish, roughly horizontally bedded siltstone (20–30 cm thick) passing into tuff–siltstone"
primary_reference: S. M. Sinitsa. 2016. Jurassic dinosaurs of Transbaikalia and prospects of searching for them in Mongolia. Paleontological Journal 50(12):1401-1411

identified_name: Kirketapel salamanquensis n. gen. n. sp.
stratcomments: Based on magnetostratigraphic, biostratigraphic and geochronologic radioisotope analyses, OR-2 is assigned to geomagnetic polarity chrons 29n (locality OR-2; 65.69–64.96Ma per\r\nGradstein et al. 2012).
primary_reference: A. Andruchow-Colombo, I. H. Escapa, and R. J. Carpenter, R. S. Hill, A. Iglesias, A. M. Abarzua, P. Wilf. 2019. Oldest record of the scale-leaved clade of Podocarpaceae, early Paleocene of Patagonia, Argentina. Alcheringa: An Australasian Journal of Palaeontology 43(1):127-145
collection_comments: A set of 24 samples from the four sections at Ormaechea and Palacio de los Loros were processed using standard palynological techniques (HCl, HF, heavy liquid ZnCl2 and HNO3) and mounted in polyvinyl alcohol at Universidad de Buenos Aires.\r\nSlides and residues are archived in the palynological collection of the Departamento de Ecología, Genética y Evolución, Facultad de Ciencias Exactas y Naturales, Universidad de Buenos Aires, as BAFCB p.m. 254–258.

geogcomments: The new collections come from two localities in the Palacio de los Loros (“Parrot Palace”) exposures of the Salamanca Formation. These crop out in the western San Jorge Basin, 36 km south of Sarmiento in southern Chubut Province, Argentina (Fig. 1).
stratcomments: Based on magnetostratigraphic, biostratigraphic and geochronologic radioisotope analyses PL-2 is assigned to geomagnetic polarity chrons 28n (64.67–63.49 Ma).
lithdescript: The uppermost Salamanca Formation contains mudstones and poorly sorted, fine grey sandstones on top of an erosive base, with infilled concave lenses and large lateral accretion sets. These rocks represent a meandering fluvial environment of low energy, with high sinuosity channels.
primary_reference: A. Andruchow-Colombo, I. H. Escapa, and R. J. Carpenter, R. S. Hill, A. Iglesias, A. M. Abarzua, P. Wilf. 2019. Oldest record of the scale-leaved clade of Podocarpaceae, early Paleocene of Patagonia, Argentina. Alcheringa: An Australasian Journal of Palaeontology 43(1):127-145

collection_comments: All identifiable material, including 1119 specimens from PL1 and 1397 from PL2, was prepared and deposited at the Museo Paleontológico Egidio Feruglio (MPEF), Trelew, Argentina.
